No, the court will likely deny the injunction. The covenant limits what structures may be built ("no structure shall be built except for dwelling purposes"), not how a lawfully built dwelling is used later, and restrictive covenants are strictly construed against restriction. The team note's reading, that the covenant's purpose of keeping the subdivision residential bars a dental office, is the main risk, since a court could read "dwelling purposes" as a general residential-use limit.

CONFIDENCE: 60
